payload.rationale: The namespace ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' has a hard limit of 500m requests.cpu. Currently, 2 running replicas of 'checkout-api' consume 200m and the benchmark-owned 'stale-canary' deployment consumes 300m, reaching the 500m cap and blocking the 3rd 'checkout-api' replica (100m request) from being admitted. Scaling the benchmark-owned 'stale-canary' (which receives no live traffic) down to 0 replicas frees 300m CPU quota, allowing 'checkout-api' to scale to its desired 3 replicas.
payload.rollback_trigger: Deployment 'checkout-api' fails to reach 3 available replicas or an error occurs.

success_criteria.description: Deployment 'checkout-api' reaches 3/3 ready and available replicas with no ReplicaFailure condition, and namespace CPU requests remain within the ResourceQuota.

critical_claims.claim: The namespace ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' has a hard limit of 500m requests.cpu and was fully saturated at 500m requests.cpu used.

The admission controller rejected pod creation for checkout-api with 'exceeded quota: case-06-cpu-budget, requested: requests.cpu=100m, used: requests.cpu=500m, limited: requests.cpu=500m', causing ReplicaSet failure.

The stale-canary deployment is labeled proofix.io/benchmark-owned='true' and proofix.io/live-traffic='false', consumed 300m CPU requests, and was scaled to zero to free quota without impacting live traffic.
The worker node vm-4 has 4 allocatable CPU cores with sufficient remaining capacity, confirming node capacity exhaustion was not the root cause.
The checkout-api service endpoints route traffic exclusively to checkout-api pods, demonstrating that stale-canary was not receiving user traffic.

closure.summary: The namespace ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' (hard limit 500m requests.cpu) was saturated because the benchmark-owned 'stale-canary' deployment consumed 300m CPU requests while active 'checkout-api' replicas consumed 200m CPU requests (total 500m), causing the Kubernetes admission controller to reject the 3rd checkout-api replica. Scaling stale-canary to 0 reclaimed the CPU quota and allowed checkout-api to achieve its desired replica count while meeting all SLO requirements.
